standard.title: Language features represent values, beliefs and attitudes
standard.description: analyse and evaluate how language features are used to implicitly or explicitly represent values, beliefs and attitudes
standard.prior_knowledge: Students analyse and evaluate how language features represent perspectives of issues, events and groups (AC9E9LY03). They have not yet analysed how language features implicitly or explicitly represent values, beliefs and attitudes.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students analyse and evaluate how language features are used to implicitly or explicitly represent values, beliefs and attitudes.

nodes.label: Explicit and implicit representation of values
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify language features that explicitly or implicitly represent values, beliefs or attitudes and analyse how they do so.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one language feature in a text that explicitly or implicitly represents a value, belief or attitude, and analyse how it does so.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse how a range of language features across a text represent values, beliefs and attitudes both explicitly and implicitly, distinguishing between the two modes of representation.
wider: Analyse social or political cartoons to identify the implicit and explicit values, beliefs and attitudes expressed through visual and language features
Compare how the same value is represented explicitly in one text and implicitly in another, examining what the different strategies achieve
Examine how language features in First Nations Australian activist texts explicitly assert values that mainstream texts represent only implicitly or not at all
nodes.hinge_reason: Node 2 requires students to evaluate how language features represent values — a judgement that depends on the ability to identify and distinguish between explicit and implicit representation. Without this distinction, evaluation collapses into surface-level comment.

response_modes.reason: The distinction between explicit and implicit representation is context-dependent — what is explicit in one cultural context may be implicit or absent in another; students need contrasting text contexts to see this clearly.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Political cartoons, activist texts and cross-cultural comparison offer rich material for value analysis — the contrast between what is said and what is assumed is particularly visible in satirical and advocacy texts.
success_criteria: Identifies at least one language feature that represents a value, belief or attitude
Distinguishes whether the representation is explicit or implicit and explains how the feature achieves it

nodes.label: Evaluating how language represents values
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can evaluate how language features are used to represent values, beliefs and attitudes, making supported judgements about the effectiveness or significance of the choices.
nodes.minimum_width: Evaluate how at least one language feature is used to represent a value or attitude in a text, making a supported judgement.
nodes.typical_width: Evaluate how language features across a text represent values, beliefs and attitudes, making supported judgements about the significance of those choices for the text's purpose and audience.
wider: Evaluate how the representation of values in political texts (e.g. election advertisements, parliamentary speeches) shapes audience understanding of what is at stake
Evaluate how values represented in media texts about First Nations Australian communities have changed over time, and assess the significance of those changes
Compare how different texts covering the same event evaluate values differently and assess what that reveals about the values of the text producers

response_modes.reason: Evaluation of how language represents values requires students to reason from specific language choices through their implicit assumptions to broader value positions — this multi-step inference needs explicit scaffolding.

success_criteria: Makes a supported judgement about how a language feature represents a value, belief or attitude
Explains the significance of that representation for the text's purpose or audience
